An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: ECf 11.3
div.ab: Quorum dum fieret collectio, clamabat ecclesia, libertatem suam reposcens; sed nichil sibi profuit.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 637 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

seg.hi: Berufung auf alte Freiheit erfindet wohl Verf. aus damaliger Gewohnheit, jede Belastung der Kirche von Wilhelm II. herzuleiten

note.seg: the appeal to ancient freedom is probably the author’s invention, from the habit of the time of tracing every burden on the Church back to William II
